title: Association of thyroid hormone therapy with quality of life and thyroid-related symptoms in patients with subclinical hypothyroidism: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Feller M, Snel M, Moutzouri E, Bauer DC, de Montmollin M, Aujesky D, et al.
population: 21 randomised trials in non-pregnant adults with subclinical hypothyroidism
funder: The Swiss National Science Foundation funded this study (grant SNSF 320030_172676 to Dr Rodondi). The funding source had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; or decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
authorConflicts: Dr Quinn was an investigator on an included trial funded by the European Union 7th Framework Program and on a trial in which the study drug was provided by Merck; Dr Stott received a research grant from the European Union 7th Framework Program.
result: Thyroid hormone lowered mean TSH into the reference range (0.5 to 3.7 against 4.6 to 14.7 mIU/l on placebo) but was not associated with benefit in general quality of life (n = 796; standardised mean difference -0.11, 95% CI -0.25 to 0.03) or thyroid-related symptoms (n = 858; SMD 0.01, -0.12 to 0.14). Risk of bias low; GRADE quality moderate to high.
